Purpose, Explanation, and Arbitrariness

span.b: 7. "If God decides what is truth and He can do as He pleases, then His will is arbitrary."

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); text-align: left;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 12px;

div.font: - "If things are true simply because God wills it, then 'truth' is subjective: just God's whim and ultimately doesn't matter."
- There is no external standard independent of God, so "truth" reduces to whatever God [subjectively] prefers.
- This makes "truth" arbitrary, as there is no "reason" for why anything is fundamentally true - and it could have been anything, if God so willed.
- Either:

div.span: - For "objective truth" to exist, then there must be an external standard above God.
- There is no "objective truth", if nothing is above God: it fundamentally reduces to God's subjective preference or power.
- God's will is fundamentally capricious - unguided by fundamental structure or consistency - as there is no external standard above God.

font.b: How the Project Addresses These Commitments

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 11px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: or 'objective truth' to exist, then there must be an external standard above God".

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: identified "truth = reality", where "reality" occurs independently from our will/preference.

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: e defined "objective" to mean "relative to something external to us", and "subjective" to mean "relative to us".

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: of these terms are defined phenomenologically - defined by our involvement (or lack thereof).

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - Thirdly, if "God's will" decides "reality", then "God's will" is the definition for "objective truth" - and "my will" is the definition for "subjective truth".

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - In other words: "objective = God's will", and "subjective = my [phenomenological] will/preference".

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - As a result, "objective truth" does not require a standard above God to exist

span.style: font-size: 11px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: - If you reject "objective = God's will", then you are rejecting "truth = reality" and/or "objective = relative to something external to us" - see the Cost of Disagreement section.

div.font: - "'Objective truth' fundamentally reduces to God's subjective preference or power".
- If we define "objective = God's will" and "subjective = my will", then it is a category error to apply the concept of "subjectivity" to God (for He is not "me").
- However, if "subjective" is redefined as "relative to any will", and "God's will = God's preference and power", then yes: this claim is true.
- In fact, with God, both objectivity and subjectivity can rationally apply without contradiction: "objective truth" is subjective, relative to God.
- In other words: "objective truth" could have been different, if God had willed differently.
- As a result, this claim is only true if "subjective" is redefined to be "relative to any will" (not just "my" own) - which encompasses "subjective = my will".

- If you reject either of these definitions, then you are using a different epistemology than this project (or reject how definitions are identified phenomenologically) - see the "This Process is Arbitrary" argument and the Cost of Disagreement section.
- "God's will is fundamentally unguided by structure or consistency, as there is no external standard above God"

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - Firstly, all definitions arise from phenomenological consistencies - see the entire Discovering Reality and Building Confidence sections.

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - Secondly, if "reality = God's will", then His will necessarily possesses consistency.

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - Note that the "God is consistent" claim is not arguing that "God's will must be monotonous or uniform in all things" - see the Defining God section.

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 4px;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - As a result, if God's will necessarily possesses consistency, then this claim becomes false.

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - "No external/forced standard" does not imply "no standard at all" - God can choose to implement His will according to a standard of His choosing.

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - If you observe consistencies in reality but don't observe consistency in God, then this is an epistemological limit, not an ontological one (ie. a result of your ignorance or lack of awareness, not because it doesn't exist).

font.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 4px;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 11px;

div.font: - If you reject this line of reasoning, then you reject the observation of any consistency at all (ontologically or epistemologically) - see all the linked sections above.
